summary: The service reads 4.2 TB per day to return 38 GB, and the top ten query patterns prune almost no granules because the ordering key leads with a UUID. Two event tables and one staging table have not been read in seven days but hold 1.8 TB. Fixing the key and adding a daily rollup would cut read volume by roughly two thirds; TTL and type changes would remove about 3.3 TB of storage.

findings.title: Ordering key leads with a UUID and prunes no granules
findings.evidence: ORDER BY (event_id, event_time). Top 10 patterns filter on tenant_id and event_type. EXPLAIN shows 12,204/12,204 granules read for the heaviest pattern.
findings.fix: Create a new table ordered by (tenant_id, event_type, event_time), backfill, then swap. Keep event_id as a column.
findings.cost_note: Accounts for about 1.9 TB/day of the 4.2 TB/day read volume.

findings.title: Three large tables have no reads in the window
findings.evidence: 0 read queries in 7 days. Combined 1.8 TB compressed across 2,140 active parts.
findings.fix: Confirm with the owner, then add a 90-day TTL and archive to object storage. Drop staging tables that are no longer used.
findings.cost_note: 1.8 TB removable at the pinned storage rate.
findings.metric: 1.8 TB of 8.4 TB stored in unread tables

findings.title: Small inserts create 4,200 parts per day
findings.evidence: Average 2,100 rows per insert, 4,200 inserts per day, 4,200 active parts and 18 concurrent merges at peak.
findings.fix: Batch to 10k–100k rows or enable async inserts with wait_for_async_insert = 1.
findings.cost_note: Reduces merge write amplification; no direct dollar saving at the current service shape.

findings.title: The same daily tenant rollup runs 38 times a day
findings.evidence: Normalized pattern 8f21c0 runs 38 times/day, reads 1.1 TB/day, and returns 2.4 MB per run.
findings.fix: Add an AggregatingMergeTree rollup keyed by (tenant_id, day) and point dashboards at it.
findings.cost_note: Removes about 1.1 TB/day of repeated reads.

findings.title: Wide types and Nullable masks inflate storage
findings.evidence: status is String at 410 GB, country is Nullable(String) at 320 GB, user_seq is UInt64 at 180 GB.
findings.fix: Use LowCardinality(String) for status and country, a non-null default for country, and UInt32 for user_seq. Verify uniqExact before applying.
findings.cost_note: Estimated 0.6–1.2 TB storage reduction after backfill.

precomputation.title: Daily tenant rollup for the dashboard pattern
precomputation.ddl:
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW events_daily
ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree
ORDER BY (tenant_id, day)
AS SELECT tenant_id, toDate(event_time) AS day, countState() AS events
FROM default.events
GROUP BY tenant_id, day;
patterns: SELECT tenant_id, toDate(event_time), count() FROM default.events GROUP BY tenant_id, day
precomputation.expected_effect: Replaces 38 scans/day of raw events (1.1 TB/day) with a scan of a rollup estimated at 2 GB.

rewrites.title: New ordering key for default.events
rewrites.why: Aligns the key with the filters used by 8 of the top 10 patterns and puts low-cardinality columns first.
rewrites.expected_effect: Cuts granules read on the heaviest patterns from 12,204 to under 400, removing about 1.9 TB/day of reads.
rewrites.measure: Run EXPLAIN indexes = 1 on the heaviest pattern before and after the backfill; compare Granules read/total.

rewrites.title: Retention for unread tables
rewrites.after:
ALTER TABLE default.legacy_orders
MODIFY TTL created_at + INTERVAL 90 DAY DELETE;
rewrites.why: Drops whole partitions instead of keeping 1.2 TB that has not been read in seven days.
rewrites.expected_effect: Removes 1.2 TB of unread storage after the first TTL merge.
rewrites.measure: SELECT formatReadableSize(sum(bytes_on_disk)) FROM system.parts WHERE active AND table = 'legacy_orders' before and after the first TTL merge.

rewrites.title: Batch inserts into default.events
rewrites.why: Server-side batching reduces part creation and merge work without changing the client schema.
rewrites.expected_effect: Cuts part creation from 4,200/day to under 300/day and reduces merge write amplification.
rewrites.measure: Compare parts created per day in system.parts and active merges in system.merges over the next 48 hours.

gaps.why: ClickHouse Cloud keeps saved queries in console metadata, not a system table. Only views and materialized views were reviewed.
The remote MCP exposes no CPU or disk metrics. The infra review uses parts, merges, cache counters and service metadata.

infrastructure.summary: Parts and merges are under control, but three large tables were never read in the window.
infrastructure.impact: Removing the unread tables frees 1.8 TB, about 21% of compressed storage.

schema.summary: The ordering key disagrees with the filters in the top patterns, and wide Nullable types inflate storage.
schema.impact: A new ordering key and tighter types cut read volume by roughly two thirds and storage by about 39%.

architecture.summary: Ingestion sends small batches, so the service spends merge work it does not need.
architecture.impact: Batching inserts cuts parts from 4,200 to under 300 per day.

queries.summary: One daily rollup is recomputed from raw data 38 times a day.
queries.impact: A daily rollup replaces 38 scans with a 2 GB read, about 1.9 TB/day less.

cost.summary: Most of the bill is storage for tables nobody reads, plus repeated scans.
cost.impact: About $81–302 per month, depending on whether a service-shape change is approved.
